If you assign a regex to a variable, like `$pattern := /[,-]/`, and use it in several `$replace` calls inside one array, the calls corrupt each other's results.
This is because every use of the variable shares one RegExp object. In `evaluateRegex`, the `result.next()` function read `re.lastIndex` when it was called, not when the match was made. If another call ran in between and moved `lastIndex`, the next match started from the wrong position.

Fix race condition with shared regex (#845)

If you assign a regex to a variable, like `$pattern := /[,-]/`, and use it in several `$replace` calls inside one array, the calls corrupt each other's results.
This is because every use of the variable shares one RegExp object. In `evaluateRegex`, the `result.next()` function read `re.lastIndex` when it was called, not when the match was made. If another call ran in between and moved `lastIndex`, the next match started from the wrong position.
The fix is to save `lastIndex` in a local variable right after `exec()` and use that saved value in
